name: Acceleration Consortium
blurb: 200-member global consortium anchoring 30+ self-driving labs for sustainable materials and molecules across health, energy, and electronics.

name: CAPeX Pioneer Center
blurb: Danish 13-year Pioneer Center accelerating Power-to-X catalyst and material discovery across DTU, Aalborg, Stanford, SLAC, Utrecht, and Toronto.

name: BIG-MAP / FULL-MAP
blurb: Battery2030+ flagship Materials Acceleration Platform for battery interfaces. BIG-MAP closed Feb 2024; successor FULL-MAP runs 2025-2029.

name: US DOE National Labs
blurb: US federal SDL funding through ARPA-E's $40M catalyst programme and CHIPS R&D's $100M semiconductor-materials programme for autonomous chemistry and electronics discovery.

name: Korea 500 SDL Initiative
blurb: MOTIE's October 2024 AI+R&D Strategy commits Korea to 500 autonomous laboratories by 2030 across nanomaterials, catalysis, organic chemistry, and bioengineering.

name: NUS AI4S · Materials Data Foundry
org: NRF Singapore · NUS I-FIM + U Toronto
blurb: Singapore's National Research Foundation AI4S programme (launched June 2026); NUS leads four of eight inaugural projects, anchored by the Materials Data Foundry (Novoselov + Aspuru-Guzik, I-FIM) building an open AI-and-robotics autonomous lab to link synthesis protocols to real-world material performance.
scale: national · 4 of 8 NUS projects · NUS–Toronto joint lab

name: UK ARIA AI Scientists
blurb: ARIA programme funding 12 AI Scientist projects testing autonomous hypothesis-to-experiment systems across drugs, batteries, quantum dots, and biology.

name: DiscoveryLabNL
blurb: Dutch shared infrastructure linking DIFFER and three TU/e institutes for autonomous materials discovery, targeting NWO LSRI submission in 2027.

name: Big Chemistry
blurb: Dutch National Growth Fund consortium of five institutes (Radboud lead, TU/e, Groningen, AMOLF, Fontys) building AI-guided self-driving labs for sustainable industrial formulations.

name: PEPR DIADEM
blurb: France 2030 programme run by CNRS, CEA, and seven academic partners, funding 51 projects that fuse AI with synthesis and characterisation across France.

name: A-Lab
blurb: Closed-loop robotic synthesis, characterisation, and ML-driven decision-making for inorganic solid-state materials, targeting 10-100x faster discovery.

name: Polybot
blurb: AI-driven autonomous platform at Argonne CNM that synthesises, prints, and tests electronic polymer films for solar cells, biosensors, and recyclable devices.

name: CMU Cloud Lab
blurb: Remote-access 24/7 facility with 200+ instruments letting researchers anywhere design and run autonomous chemistry, biology, and materials experiments.

name: Coscientist
blurb: LLM-driven agent from Gabe Gomes' group that reads literature, plans syntheses, and controls liquid-handling robots from natural-language prompts.

name: Abolhasani Lab
blurb: Self-driving fluidic lab combining microreactor flow chemistry, robotics, and AI to accelerate perovskite quantum dots and energy-relevant materials.

name: Genesis
blurb: Ross King's third-generation Robot Scientist programme pursuing fully automated hypothesis generation and testing across biology and chemistry.

name: Cooper Group / MIF Liverpool
blurb: Andy Cooper's mobile robot chemists roam the Materials Innovation Factory, autonomously running photocatalyst, porous-material, and CO₂-capture experiments; the £81M MIF opened in 2017, building on the robotic Centre for Materials Discovery running since 2007.

name: HELMA (Helmholtz Acceleration Alliance)
blurb: KIT-led Helmholtz consortium positioning Germany's autonomous SDLs for health, energy storage, catalysis, and electronics in smart data centres.

name: BioPACIFIC MIP
blurb: NSF Materials Innovation Platform at UCSB and UCLA offering free peer-reviewed access to automated, AI-driven synthesis and characterisation of bio-derived materials.

name: Cusp AI (Cambridge HQ)
blurb: AI-driven materials discovery startup (Max Welling co-founder) designing functional crystals on demand for carbon capture, batteries, PFAS removal, and semiconductors.

name: Cusp AI (Amsterdam node)
blurb: Amsterdam Science Park (Lab42) node of CuspAI running the Welling-led ML stack for generative inverse design of functional materials.

name: AMADAP
blurb: Brabec group platform spanning high-throughput synthesis, SPINBOT spin-coating, and the AMANDA device line to autonomously discover emerging photovoltaic materials.

name: NIMS Autonomous AI Network
blurb: NIMS-Tsukuba framework letting multiple autonomous AI labs spontaneously share data and coordinate searches across different material systems.

name: dLab
blurb: Hitosugi-group digital lab chaining thin-film synthesis with XRD, Raman, conductivity, and optics for fully automated standardised materials data.

name: KAIST-POSCO Autonomous Lab
blurb: Dong-Hwa Seo's industry-academia autonomous lab with POSCO N.EX.T Hub cutting battery cathode discovery time by 93 percent.

name: KIST MARK System
blurb: KIST's robotic synthesis + characterisation + ML workflow for accelerated discovery across battery and functional materials.

name: SNU SDL Ecosystem
blurb: Yousung Jung's group uses LLMs to predict material synthesisability, anchoring a wider SNU autonomous-lab cluster across batteries and catalysis.

name: Jun Jiang Group / ChemAgents + Robot Chemist
blurb: Robotic AI-Chemist 2.0 lineage couples on-board LLM multi-agent ChemAgents with cloud-linked lab robots for autonomous chemistry.

name: Noël Group
blurb: Flow chemistry group running RoboChem, an autonomous photocatalytic reaction platform that optimises continuous-flow photochemistry without human intervention.

name: DIFFER Autonomous Energy Materials Discovery (Süleyman Er)
blurb: Computational group screening energy materials (redox-flow electrolytes, electrocatalysts) via high-throughput DFT plus ML over public chemical databases.

name: Lila Sciences
blurb: Flagship Pioneering venture building Scientific Superintelligence: AI agents coupled to autonomous wet labs across therapeutics, materials, energy, and chemicals.

name: Medra AI
blurb: Physical AI scientists for life-science labs: vision-guided robot arms operating standard instruments end-to-end across gene editing, cell biology, and microbial discovery.

name: Periodic Labs
blurb: Stealth-emerged lab building AI scientists with paired autonomous laboratories, starting with materials physics: superconductors and semiconductor thermal materials.

name: XtalPi 晶泰科技
blurb: HKEX-listed AI + quantum-physics + robotics platform running autonomous drug-discovery and materials labs across Shenzhen, Shanghai, and Boston.

name: LabGenius
blurb: Bermondsey biotech whose EVA platform closed-loops ML design with automated wet-lab cycles to engineer selectivity-enhanced antibodies for solid tumours.

name: Deep Principle 深度原理
blurb: Agentic AI for materials and chemistry. ECML framework orchestrates DFT, MD, ML, and wet-lab experiments; recently hired MIT's Heather Kulik as Chief Scientist.

name: Qingkui 青葵智造
blurb: Beijing-registered robotics-plus-AI scale-up building chemistry workstations for pharma, energy, and advanced materials; planning a 100-robot AI cloud lab in Yichang.

name: Yongjiang Lab 甬江实验室
blurb: Zhejiang provincial materials research institute running advanced functional, structural, and transformative materials platforms including a 6-inch micro-nano device line.

name: DP Technology / Bohrium 深势科技
blurb: AI-for-Science company behind Bohrium, Hermite, Piloteye, and Uni-Lab, building foundation-model infrastructure for chemistry, biology, and batteries.

name: Jiageng Innovation Lab 嘉庚创新实验室
blurb: Provincial mega-institute building China's first dedicated energy-storage research infrastructure, spanning low-carbon energy, displays, and graphene.

name: Shanghai AI Laboratory
blurb: National AGI lab whose AGI4S programme builds Intern-S1 scientific foundation models and the Intern-Discovery agent-plus-instrument platform.

name: ByteDance Seed AI4S
blurb: ByteDance's foundation-model team applying AI to biological structure prediction (Protenix), quantum chemistry, and topological materials physics.

name: DeepH (Duan Group)
blurb: Tsinghua physics group developing DeepH, a universal neural-network DFT Hamiltonian model accelerating electronic-structure prediction across arbitrary material structures.

name: SurFF / Uni-MOF (Wang Group)
blurb: Xiaonan Wang's group building foundation models (SurFF, Uni-MOF) for catalyst surfaces and MOF gas adsorption at high-throughput screening scale.

name: Novartis MicroCycle
blurb: Novartis Basel in-house self-driving lab integrating micro-scale synthesis, automated purification, real-time bioassays, and ML-driven compound design.

name: Chemspeed / SciY
blurb: Swiss lab-automation vendor selling modular robotic synthesis, formulation, and characterisation workflows for materials, pharma, and battery R&D.

name: Fraunhofer MAPs
blurb: Fraunhofer ISC programme coupling robotic synthesis and characterisation with AI-driven design for glass, battery, and functional materials.

name: Emerald Cloud Lab
blurb: Remote-controlled cloud laboratory letting scientists design and run wet-lab experiments on 200+ instrument models via a unified software interface.

name: Ginkgo Bioworks
blurb: Synthetic-biology platform offering autonomous strain-engineering foundries and cloud-lab access for antibody, enzyme, and cell-line programmes.

name: CMU AI Science Foundry
blurb: Carnegie Mellon initiative running the ASAP autonomous platform for AI-guided experiments in hard materials, chemistry, and biology.

name: Strateos
blurb: Cloud-lab-as-a-service operating robotic San Diego and Menlo Park facilities for remote small-molecule, biologics, and synthetic-biology workflows.

name: Kebotix
blurb: Self-driving lab platform pairing generative chemistry, automated synthesis, and robotic characterisation for specialty-chemicals and advanced-materials discovery.

name: Arctoris
blurb: Oxford-based automated drug-discovery CRO running the Ulysses robotic platform for reproducible biochemical, cell, and molecular assay data.

name: Culture Biosciences
blurb: Cloud-connected 250 mL bioreactor service for outsourced upstream bioprocess development with remote monitoring and bioprocess software.

name: Automata (LINQ)
blurb: LINQ platform orchestrates modular benchtop robotics with a node-based workflow canvas and Python SDK for genomics and assay screening.

name: Benchling
blurb: Cloud R&D platform combining ELN, registry, inventory, and workflow tools for biotech, used by most large biopharma.

name: Artificial
blurb: aLab Suite orchestrates instruments, robots, people, and data into closed-loop digital workflows for life-science labs (Palo Alto, USA · Microsoft M12-backed).

name: Synthace
blurb: Digital experiment platform for designing, simulating, and executing high-dimensional multivariate experiments on lab automation hardware.

name: Unchained Labs (Stuntman)
blurb: Stuntman is a natural-language AI automation platform with flexible hardware for biologics, gene therapy, and reaction screening.

name: UniteLabs
blurb: Python-based lab automation OS connecting 175+ instruments through one API for code-defined, version-controlled workflows.

name: Cenevo (Titian + Labguru)
blurb: Post-merger entity behind Mosaic sample tracking and Labguru ELN/LIMS, integrating 150+ instruments across biopharma R&D.

name: HighRes + Opentrons
blurb: Modular robotic workcells and Cellario scheduling software paired with Opentrons via a 2026 agent-to-agent AI workflow partnership.

name: Atinary
blurb: SDLabs no-code platform pairing Bayesian and ML optimizers with robotic hardware for closed-loop chemistry and materials discovery.

name: ABB Robotics
blurb: Industrial robotics arm supplying GoFa and YuMi collaborative arms plus AVR autonomous mobile robots for multi-vendor lab workcells.

name: Jensen Lab
blurb: MIT ChemE group integrating flow reactors, robotics, online analytics, and machine learning into autonomous platforms for reaction discovery and process development.

name: Cronin Group / Chemify
blurb: Glasgow group behind the Chemputer and chemputation: synthesis encoded as executable code on universal robotic platforms, commercialised through spinout Chemify.

name: Grzybowski Group / IBS-CARS
blurb: IBS Center for Algorithmic and Robotized Synthesis pairing AI retrosynthesis (Chematica/Synthia) with closed-loop chemical robotics.

name: MMLI / Burke Group
blurb: NSF-funded institute around Burke's iterative MIDA-boronate small-molecule synthesizer, closing the loop with AI agents like AlphaSynthesis.

name: Hein Lab / Telescope
blurb: UBC spinout commercialising self-driving process-chemistry platforms (IvoryOS, DirectInject-LC) for pharma, critical minerals, and Acceleration Consortium partners.

name: Ley Group
blurb: Cambridge group pioneering continuous-flow and machine-assisted synthesis for natural products and methodology, with four spinouts and 900+ publications.

name: Doyle Group
blurb: UCLA catalysis group fusing nickel cross-coupling, photocatalysis, and machine-learning reaction optimisation through founding roles in BioLEC and C-CAS centres.

name: Hamilton Company
blurb: Reno-based manufacturer of Microlab liquid-handling robots, process sensors, and automated sample-storage systems used across pharma and clinical labs.

name: Opentrons
blurb: Open-source liquid-handling robots and the Flex workstation plus OpentronsAI natural-language protocol design for genomics and proteomics labs.

name: Tecan Group
blurb: Swiss-listed maker of Fluent and Freedom EVO liquid-handling platforms plus OEM components for diagnostics and life-science automation.

name: Peak Analysis & Automation
blurb: UK lab-automation integrator building modular robotic workcells with Overlord scheduling software for life-science and pharma throughput.

name: NSF AI Institute for Materials Innovation
blurb: First NSF AI institute dedicated to materials, coordinating closed-loop autonomous experimentation across Cornell, Princeton, CCNY, and Boston University.

name: Radical AI
blurb: AI agents coupled to a closed-loop robotic lab discovering inorganic materials, alloys, and electrolytes; CSO Gerbrand Ceder built LBNL's A-Lab.

name: Mattiq
blurb: Northwestern spinout running high-throughput combinatorial megalibrary synthesis of millions of nanomaterials per day to train AI for clean-energy catalysts.

name: NRC BattMAP / BattPAP
blurb: National Research Council Canada self-driving labs for battery-materials discovery and critical-mineral processing under the Critical Battery Materials Initiative.

name: AIChemy (UK AI for Chemistry Hub)
blurb: £12M EPSRC national hub (Liverpool + Imperial) developing AI-planned robotic and autonomous chemistry, including mobile robot scientists for exploratory synthesis.

name: Dunia Innovations
blurb: Self-driving labs running the full design-make-test-analyse loop for electrocatalyst, battery, and CO2-conversion materials, scaling to a €280M Berlin GigaLab.

name: AURORA (KTH)
blurb: Modular robotic platform integrating automated synthesis, characterisation, and evaluation, demonstrated on metal-halide perovskites.

name: CELEST Autonomous Battery Lab
blurb: Fully automated, AI-planned battery-materials lab that autonomously synthesises, assembles, and cycles cells.

name: EPFL Self-Driving Lab (LIAC)
blurb: Self-driving platform for nano- and advanced-materials synthesis with active-learning optimisation.

name: ChemLex
blurb: 24/7 fully automated robotic synthesis line (~800 reactions/day) coupling AI to wet-lab chemistry for drug discovery.

name: RIKEN / IST Maholo SDL
blurb: JST-funded national self-driving lab (Maholo robotic-arm platform) for closed-loop materials discovery, with a prototyping lab at RIKEN BDR Kobe and a demonstrator at Institute of Science Tokyo.

name: AIST AUTOkobo
blurb: AIST's Multi-Modal AI lab-automation initiative for autonomous experimentation, now spanning all seven AIST research departments.

name: KIMS Autonomous Alloy Lab
blurb: Closed-loop alloy discovery (arc-melting to annealing to XRD) with reinforcement-learning optimisation.

name: KIER Smart Laboratory
blurb: 24-hour autonomous synthesis, analysis, and XRD for safety-critical energy and catalyst materials.

name: MegaRobo 镁伽科技
blurb: China's largest smart-lab robotics company, building autonomous agents that run real experiments across life sciences, chemistry, and energy materials.

name: FutureHouse / Edison Scientific
blurb: AI-scientist agent stack (the Robin multi-agent discovery system) coupled to its own robotic wet lab; for-profit spinout Edison.

name: ASCEND
blurb: BMFTR-funded consortium led by Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin and the Fritz Haber Institute (with BASF, Siemens Energy, Dunia Innovations, and TU Berlin/BasCat) running AI-guided self-driving labs, high-throughput characterisation, and digital twins to accelerate catalyst discovery for sustainable chemistry.
scale: AI closed-loop catalyst SDLs + digital twins

name: AI-Assisted Materials Discovery Institute
blurb: Institute announced in 2026 at Tsinghua University, to be led by Nobel laureate Omar Yaghi, pairing AI with reticular chemistry for materials discovery; at concept stage, with no facility details public yet.

name: NSF PCL Test Bed
blurb: NSF national network of AI-enabled programmable cloud laboratories: ~$380M to 20 teams over four years plus Astera Institute matching, anchored by nodes like Penn State's LATTICE thin-film SDL with Argonne.

name: SOLVE Chemistry
blurb: London SDL flow lab pairing online-UHPLC high-throughput experimentation with Bayesian optimisation for predictive process chemistry and right-first-time scale-up.

name: Matter Lab
blurb: Alán Aspuru-Guzik's group; originated the modern SDL field with ChemOS (2017) and spun out Kebotix, Atinary, and the Acceleration Consortium.

name: IMDEA Materials SDL
blurb: Haranczyk group self-driving lab for automated polymer processing (melt and solution workflows), serving six Madrid research groups and the Materials-Commons EU network.

name: Ewha IMMS Self-Driving Lab
blurb: Korea's MSIT / NRL 2.0 national research laboratory at Ewha Womans University (director Hoi Ri Moon); a 330 m² self-driving lab with ten function-based workstations across five material classes, a Bayesian-optimisation and LLM-agent decision layer, moving to open-access user operation from 2028.

name: IPRD
org: Institute of Process Research and Development
blurb: Institute of Process Research and Development, University of Leeds.

name: Swiss Cat+
blurb: ETH Domain-funded national catalysis infrastructure jointly operated by EPFL and ETH Zurich, combining robotic high-throughput experimentation, AI-guided experimental design, and automated workflows to enable self-driving laboratories for catalyst discovery and optimization across homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
scale: High throughput analytical platform (LC, LC-PREP, SQ-MS, IM-Q-TOF, MIR & FIR FT-IR, Chiral-SFC, 400 MHz NMR, desktop NMR)

name: ODACell
org: Ångström Advanced Battery Centre (ÅABC) · Uppsala University
blurb: Self-driving battery laboratory developed at Uppsala University's Ångström Advanced Battery Centre, integrating automated electrolyte formulation, robotic coin-cell assembly, in-line cycling, computer vision, and Bayesian optimization for closed-loop electrolyte discovery.

name: Aurora (Empa)
org: Empa (Battaglia Lab, Materials for Energy Conversion)
blurb: Battaglia Lab's autonomous robotic battery-materials platform automating electrolyte formulation, cell assembly, and cycling on >1200 cycler channels, with ontologized FAIR data management.

name: Ophelia (Empa)
org: Empa (Battaglia Lab, Materials for Energy Conversion)
blurb: Battaglia Lab platform running 8 parallel CO₂-electrolysis reactors for gas-diffusion electrodes with automated online gas and liquid product analysis, published as an open blueprint.

name: ARES (AFRL)
blurb: The Air Force Research Laboratory's Autonomous Research System (Maruyama): ARES OS was the first major infrastructure package for SDL deployment, demonstrated on autonomous carbon-nanotube growth.

name: CAMEO (NIST)
blurb: NIST's closed-loop autonomous system (Kusne) running Bayesian phase mapping jointly with property optimisation live on synchrotron beamlines, with opt-in human collaboration.

name: MINERVA (BAM)
blurb: BAM's modular robotic platform (Rühle group) for synthesis, purification, and in-line characterisation of nano- and advanced materials (seven materials across five classes), with ELN/LIMS integration via OpenBIS.

name: BEAR (Brown Lab, BU)
blurb: Keith Brown's Bayesian experimental autonomous researcher: closed-loop additive manufacturing and mechanical-design experiments, one of the field's flagship SDL architectures.

name: MAOSIC (CUHK-Shenzhen)
blurb: The first cloud-SDL demonstration: Xi Zhu's materials acceleration operating system in cloud, which autonomously discovered chiral inorganic perovskite nanocrystals via remote collaboration.

name: AI4Mat Initiative | Hip Lab
blurb: Kedar Hippalgaonkar's initiative integrating AI, robotics, and agentically driven high-throughput experiments for functional energy and electronic materials, backed by a S$25M MTI Programmatic Award and the S$10M Mat-GDT platform.

name: ChemTech Lab
blurb: Connor Taylor's self-driving laboratory for drug discovery and chemical process development, funded through a £2M RAEng research fellowship.

name: MAITENA (CIC energiGUNE)
blurb: Automation and AI platform for inorganic energy materials combining automated co-precipitation, solvothermal, and sol-gel synthesis with XRD and electrochemical characterisation and active-learning experiment design.

name: QPillars
blurb: Zurich startup making lab instruments agent-ready through MCP servers and SiLA 2 drivers, so AI copilots can turn natural-language requests into validated, reproducible instrument workflows.

name: Shenzhen Synthetic Biology Infrastructure
blurb: CAS SIAT-led national major science infrastructure at Guangming Science City: modular fully-automated workcells running the synthetic-biology design-build-test-learn loop at high throughput, open to academic and industrial users.

name: ZJU iBioFoundry + iChemFoundry
blurb: Zhejiang University's twin automated science installations at the Hangzhou Innovation Center — a synthetic-biology iBioFoundry and a molecular-manufacturing iChemFoundry, 300+ instruments across 14,000 m², operated as shared platforms.

name: AITHYRA
org: Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW) · Vienna BioCenter
blurb: Austrian Academy of Sciences institute for biomedical AI under founding director Michael Bronstein, building a closed-loop AI-driven robotics lab: vision-enabled liquid handlers, self-teaching robotic arms, and sensor-rich work cells under an AI orchestration layer, with 100 m² in phase I at the Marxbox and 400 m² in the purpose-built Vienna BioCenter building.
scale: AI-driven robotics lab · 100 m² phase I → 400 m² phase II · 10–14 groups

name: AI BioDesign (Allen Institute)
org: Allen Institute + UW + Fred Hutch · Fund for Science and Technology
blurb: Open-science accelerator with the University of Washington and Fred Hutch designing proteins and genes that do not exist in nature; bench teams run massively parallel library experiments while a machine-learning team chooses each next round, scored on how much the models improved. Scale comes from parallelising inside the test tube rather than from robotics.
scale: accelerator · massively parallel in-tube libraries (scale not from robotics)

name: CircuLab
org: Stockholm University · WISE Research Technology Platform
blurb: WISE Research Technology Platform at Stockholm University for circular and sustainable materials: automated synthesis and processing, real-time monitoring of emissions, hazardous chemicals and physicochemical change, and ML plus Bayesian-optimisation decision making across four clusters and about 20 instruments; open to academia, start-ups, and industry.
scale: 4 clusters · ~20 instruments · open to academia, start-ups, industry
investLabel: WISE + Stockholm University (part of SEK 136M over 4 platforms)

name: BESSY III
blurb: HZB's 4th-generation soft-to-tender X-ray source for Berlin-Adlershof, planned from the ground up around intelligent autonomous experimentation, AI-supported sample synthesis and handling, and FAIR data, with synthesis and characterisation laboratories on the same integrated research campus; CDR due 2027, construction from 2032, operations mid-2030s.
scale: 4th-gen soft X-ray source · CDR 2027 · operations mid-2030s
